subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Uneven Roasting
description: A quick, practical guide to Uneven Roasting.

hook.text: Break open a poorly roasted bean and you might find the outside is brown while the inside is still pale and raw.

buildup.text: Uneven roasting means heat didn't penetrate uniformly. The surface over-developed while the core under-developed.

discovery.text: This creates a mix of sour (raw center) and bitter (over-roasted exterior) flavors in the same cup—a chaotic taste.

twist.text: Uneven roasting often comes from inconsistent bean size. Large and small beans in the same batch develop at different rates.

climax.text: Screen-grading green coffee (sorting by size) before roasting is a simple fix that dramatically improves consistency.

punchline.text: Same batch, different roasts inside every bean. Sorting solves this.

quiz.question: What causes uneven roasting within a single bean?
options: Heat didn't penetrate uniformly—surface over-roasted, core under-developed
